Subject: RE: Capacity add mid-term + co-term question

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answer: we can support the uplift with two pragmatic paths that avoid a single-year catch-up invoice and keep you aligned to the Mar 31 co-term. I attached a short matrix (staggered_pricing_matrix.xlsx) that shows the math; summary below.

Option 1 — Prorated immediate uplift to co-term
- We apply the full uplift now but prorate the charge to your Mar 31 co-term (you only pay for days used until co-term).
- On Mar 31 we annualize the new commit moving forward.
- Pros: simple invoicing, immediate capacity. Cons: may still show a noticeable mid-term line item.

Option 2 — Staggered voucher / installment approach (recommended)
- We issue a set of prepaid vouchers equal to the uplift value, split over 3 or 6 monthly installments (you choose).
- Vouchers are consumed against invoices as usage accrues; any unused voucher balance rolls into the co-term annualization on Mar 31.
- Pros: spreads budget impact across months, preserves predictable MRR profile for your finance team.
- Cons: small operational coordination to apply vouchers on each invoice.

Operational notes:
- SLA and burst remain unchanged for both options; we can add a short-term burst quota if you expect spikes.
- We can produce an interim invoice + voucher schedule for your procurement team.
- I CC'd Ben to confirm billing treatment and Marissa for procurement/SOW updates.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm preferred voucher cadence (3 or 6 months) and if NovaBio can accept vouchers as prepaid credits.
2) We draft a short SOW amendment + invoice schedule; sign via DocuSign.
3) We spin up additional capacity the day after the signed amendment.

I've attached the pricing matrix and your Q3 usage. Happy to hop on a 20-min call to run numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Quick accounting note from our side: for the voucher approach we classify vouchers as prepaid credits on the customer's account. For NovaBio that typically results in:
- Initial activation invoice (if you choose a partial upfront payment) recorded as revenue when the capacity becomes available.
- Voucher purchases recorded as deferred revenue and recognized over the period the vouchers are consumed against invoices (matches usage).

I'll work with your finance team to provide a 1-page memo that your accounting team can use for internal treatment — simple language, not legal advice.

Proposed commercial path to expedite procurement:
- 10% activation fee invoiced on signing (covers immediate capacity and provisioning).
- Remaining uplift value split into 3 monthly voucher invoices (recommended).
- SOW amendment (stub attached) references optional Dedicated pool next year; no obligation now.

If that works, Marissa can push a PO-friendly SOW and I can generate the invoice schedule.
